transcript: Every year, about 8 million tons of plastic flow into the world's oceans That equals one truckload every minute In the Pacific Ocean, a huge area of garbage twice the size of Texas is floating Called the Great Pacific Garbage Patch Debris carried by the currents has gathered there over many years Larger pieces of plastic Broken down by waves and ultraviolet light Slowly becomes micro-plastic These tiny particles enter the food chain From plankton to fish And eventually onto our dinner tables The impact on marine life is severe Whales and seabirds have mistaken plastic bags for food and have died after swallowing them Coral reefs too face the double threat of chemical pollution and warming waters Governments around the world have introduced various policies such as charging for plastic bags and banning certain plastics companies on the other hand have invested in biodegradable materials and recycling technology. In the end, the problem will be solved by the choices each of us makes. Reduce, reuse, recycle. The accumulation of small choices in daily Life will change the future of the ocean

segments.text: Every year, about 8 million tons of plastic flow into the world's oceans
That equals one truckload every minute
In the Pacific Ocean, a huge area of garbage twice the size of Texas is floating
Called the Great Pacific Garbage Patch
Debris carried by the currents has gathered there over many years
Broken down by waves and ultraviolet light Slowly becomes micro-plastic
These tiny particles enter the food chain From plankton to fish
And eventually onto our dinner tables The impact on marine life is severe
Whales and seabirds have mistaken plastic bags for food
and have died after swallowing them
Coral reefs too face the double threat
of chemical pollution and warming waters
Governments around the world have introduced various policies
such as charging for plastic bags and banning certain plastics
companies on the other hand have invested in biodegradable
